# Model folder, param.yaml and deployment

## Folder contract (what `app_edgeai.py` loads)
```
<name>/ model/{model.onnx [, model.prototxt]}  artifacts/{subgraph_0_tidl_net.bin, subgraph_0_tidl_io_1.bin, allowedNode.txt,
        onnxrtMetaData.txt, *.layer_info.txt ...}  param.yaml  dataset.yaml
```
Naming follows TI zoo (`ONR-<TASK>-<nnnn>-<description>`: ONR = ONNX runtime; OD detection, CL classification, SS segmentation).
Pick an unused number (zoo uses 6xxx-8xxx; use 9xxx for your own).

## param.yaml by task (generated by `package_model.py` from the TI zoo templates)
Common: `session.{session_name: onnxrt, target_device: <device name, e.g. TDA4VM>, model_path, artifacts_folder, input_details, output_details,
input_optimization: true}`, `task_type`, `preprocess.{resize, crop, reverse_channels, resize_with_pad, data_layout: NCHW, pad_color}`.

| | detection | classification | segmentation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preprocess.resize / crop` | `[H, W]` both | ints: resize S, crop C (centre crop) | `[H, W]` both |
| `resize_with_pad` | `[false, corner]` (TI's gst path never pads) | false | false |
| `pad_color` | `[114,114,114]` | 0 | 0 |
| `postprocess` | `DetectionBoxSL2BoxLS` formatter, `normalized_detections: false` | `{}` | `{}` |
| outputs | `dets [N,5]` float, `labels [N]` int64 | scores `[1,K]` float | class map, uint8 if ArgMax |
| `metric.label_offset_pred` | `{i: i+1}` | - | - |

Rules that cost time:
- List-valued `resize`/`crop` are `[HEIGHT, WIDTH]` (the app reverses them). Wrong order -> `Got invalid dimensions for input`.
- `resize_with_pad` true makes post-processing undo a pad that never happened if the pipeline squashes.
- `reverse_channels: true` -> the app builds `tiovxdlpreproc ... tensor-format=1` (BGR): right for BGR-trained models (e.g. YOLOX); use
  `--channels rgb` (false) for RGB-trained models (torchvision-style).
- Input/outputs names/shapes/types are read from the ONNX by `package_model.py`; if the input is not uint8 it warns (TI's pipeline feeds
  uint8 with normalisation folded in).
- `dataset.yaml`: categories with ids from 1; detection `label_offset_pred` maps zero-based class index to them.

## Deploy
```bash
BOARD=root@<board-ip> GST_SOC=<key> scripts/deploy_to_board.sh pkg/<name> <config.yaml>
```
- Uploads to a staging folder, then moves it to `/opt/model_zoo/<name>` and the config to `/opt/edgeai-gst-apps/configs/`.
- **Never deletes.** If the model or config already exists the script stops (exit 3) and changes nothing; `REPLACE=1` moves the old one
  to `.backup-<name>-<time>` first, so you can restore it (`mv`) or delete it yourself later.
- Both destinations (model folder and config name) are checked before anything is uploaded, so a collision changes nothing.
- Runs `SOC=$GST_SOC ./app_edgeai.py` under `timeout` and exits with the result: 0 ok; 5 smoke test failed. Success needs evidence: exit 0
  (or, with `LIVE=1`, the expected timeout), a non-empty log, no known error line, and `Offloaded Nodes - N, Total Nodes - N` with N == M
  (`ALLOW_PARTIAL_OFFLOAD=1` accepts fewer but never zero; `NO_OFFLOAD_CHECK=1` skips). A finite input must finish within `RUN_SECONDS`.
  The log cannot prove frames were processed: set `EXPECT_OUTPUT='<remote glob>'` to require a file written during the run.
- Other exit codes: 2 bad model folder, 3 destination exists, 4 copy failed. Config source: `ti-edgeai-generate-config`.

## Look at the output
Copy output frames back (`scp root@<ip>:/opt/edgeai-test-data/output/<file> .`) and check: detector boxes on the objects, not stretched
(aspect mismatch) or uniformly shifted (padding flag); none at all (threshold, label offset, channel order); classifier labels plausible.
Delete test outputs afterwards, and temporary model folders only when you created them (never a folder you did not upload).

## Controls
A zoo model run through the same config is the control: zoo works but yours does not -> suspect your artifacts/version; both fail ->
environment (SOC, services, memory). `board_host_check.py` separates "device differs from host" (runtime equivalence on identical tensors) from "model is just inaccurate"
(task accuracy); neither tells you whether the application's own preprocessing is right.
